discussion_comments.comment_body:
Looked at where SESSION_EXTENSIONS_LOADED is dispatched (useChatStream.ts): the cached path dispatches it synchronously inside the load effect, and the cold path dispatches it after resumeAgent({ load_model_and_extensions: true }) resolves. The trigger's visibility was gated on isSessionExtensionsLoaded, which was only ever set from that event handler, so when this component doesn't observe the event (e.g. the synchronous cached dispatch can fire before the listener is re-attached on a session switch) the icon stays hidden. That's #9749.

That's also why gating the toggles on the event (the "visible but non-mutating until the load event" option) would re-introduce the original symptom for the switches: the same event is the unreliable part here, so toggles could stay disabled indefinitely on exactly the session switches #9749 is about.

The cold-resume window you describe is real, and this change does widen it: exposing the menu during resumeAgent lets a toggle reach /agent/*_extension while load_extensions_from_session is still applying the resumed set. But that ordering hazard between a user mutation and the initial session load is a backend sequencing concern (crates/goose/src/agents/agent.rs), and there's no reliable "resume in progress" signal exposed to this component today.

Proposal: keep this PR scoped to the visibility regression in #9749 (covered by the new test) and handle the toggle-during-resume race separately. Happy to open a follow-up issue for the backend sequencing, or to gate the switches here if there's a reliable resume-in-progress signal to key off.
**Fixed in aa4bcda070a.** The bootstrap now only applies the persisted effort if the user has not touched the Intelligence dropdown, so a slow config read cannot clobber an in-flight selection.
